title: Staff Platform Engineer, Agentic Engineering
descriptionHtml:
The AI orchestration of your wildest imagination.

n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact.

Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve:

  • Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders

  • Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects

  • Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation


That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register.

We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.

Staff Platform Engineer, Agentic Engineering

Developer Productivity · AI Coding Agents · Developer Platform

Our ambition: an engineering organisation where humans and agents work as one continuously learning system, turning frontier AI capabilities and real-world feedback into more ambitious product development. We want n8n to be the reference for how this is done, without compromising quality, resilience or trust. Your main goal is to make that real.

This is a Staff individual contributor role in Developer Platform and the technical driving force behind ACDC (Agent-centric Development Cycle), our engineering-wide initiative for agentic development. Nobody has a playbook for this yet. You'll write ours.

You won't start from zero. Agents wired into Linear already automate around 80% of the development cycle on one of our developer platform projects, alongside pilots for insight, feature-flag and PR-review agents and a shared agent harness. Your job is to take this from promising experiments to the way n8n builds software.

This role is for someone who thinks about this problem constantly. You run agents all day, rebuild your own workflow every time the frontier moves, and have more ideas than time.

You'll stay hands-on, building the first versions yourself, and shape how the work grows beyond one person.

What you'll do

Set direction and own the outcome

  • Identify where agentic development can make the greatest difference, using developer feedback, existing experiments and engineering performance data.

  • Set the strategy and priorities across agent execution, repository readiness, CI, security and developer workflows.

  • Make build, buy or pass decisions on tools and vendors, and own the cost and value trade-offs, including AI spend.

  • Make decisions where requirements are incomplete and the trade-offs between autonomy, reliability, security and review effort are still emerging.

  • Build alignment through technical proposals, clear decisions and working software, and report progress and impact to engineering leadership.

Build the foundations

  • Design and build isolated execution environments where agents can work with the right access to code, tools and context, without exposing secrets or sensitive systems.

  • Own the safety model: which task categories agents may attempt, what they must never touch, and where human review is required, partnering with Security on sensitive areas like auth, billing, permissions and data handling.

  • Make n8n's monorepo agent-ready, working with Architecture and senior engineers on repo structure, testability, boundaries and the context agents need.

Integrate agents into how we work

  • Build repeatable workflows that take Linear issues through agent execution, self-verification and review to merged PRs, across a growing range of task types.

  • Integrate agentic workflows with GitHub, CI, test infrastructure and code review, so the agentic path becomes the easiest path for engineers.

  • Extend the loop beyond coding: connect earlier signals like product research and customer requests, and later ones like production metrics, so agents contribute across the whole cycle.

  • Open it up beyond engineering, so PMs, designers and others can turn a well-defined issue into a reviewed, mergeable change.

  • Shape review practices, such as PR evidence that shows what changed, what ran, what risks remain and where human judgment is needed.

Measure what works

  • Build benchmarks from real historical engineering tasks to evaluate output quality, failure modes, review burden and production risk.

  • Define and track quality and adoption signals, such as reviewer acceptance rate, CI pass rate, rework rate and developer satisfaction.

  • Use data and feedback to change course, retire what doesn't work, and build trust across engineering.

Requirements

Must-haves

  • 🔥 Frontier obsession: You live at the frontier. You try new models and tools as they land, and you have strong, evidence-backed opinions on what's real and what's hype.

  • 🧭 Staff-scope ownership: You’ve led complex platform, DevEx or engineering productivity initiatives across teams, from defining the problem to sustained adoption and measurable impact, where there was no established approach to follow.

  • 🤖 Agentic depth: You use coding agents daily as a power user, and you've built infrastructure around them, such as repo context and instructions, tool or MCP integrations, sandboxed execution or agent workflows in CI, that other engineers rely on.

  • 🎯 Product mindset for internal platforms: You treat engineers as your customers. You start from real friction, prioritise by impact, make build-vs-buy calls, weigh cost against value, and let adoption tell you whether something works.

  • 🤝 Direction without authority: You've set technical direction that multiple teams followed, through proposals, design reviews and credibility with senior engineers across Platform, Product Engineering, AI, Security and Architecture.

  • 🔐 Safety judgment: You've made real decisions on permissions, secrets, sandboxing, sensitive code paths and human-in-the-loop review, and can explain the trade-offs.

  • 📊 Measurement that drives decisions: You've built evaluations, benchmarks or quality metrics and used them to change course or retire things that didn't work. You care about outcomes, not lines of AI-generated code.

  • ✍️ Writing that changes decisions: Your technical proposals and documentation have shifted what teams did.

Nice-to-haves

  • 📦 TypeScript monorepos: You have worked in a large TypeScript, Node.js or JavaScript monorepo.

  • ⚙️ Developer platforms: You have experience with GitHub Actions, Linear, test infrastructure, preview environments or internal developer platforms.

  • 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Growing a team: You've mentored engineers or helped shape a new team as an initiative grew beyond one person.

  • 🌍 Open-source communities: You have contributed to open-source or source-available projects with active developer communities.

  • 🏢 B2B SaaS context: You understand environments where reliability, permissions, data handling and customer trust are central.

  • 🔗 Workflow automation: You're familiar with workflow automation, integration platforms, AI orchestration or developer-facing products.

Why join us?

At n8n, you'll define how autonomous AI agents become a trusted part of engineering inside one of Europe's fastest-growing AI-native infrastructure companies. Your work will shape the platform foundations, safety model, evaluation framework and developer workflows that decide whether agents can contribute meaningfully to production engineering without lowering the quality bar.

You'll join a remote-first team with high autonomy, high visibility and a strong builder mindset. Because this is a first-of-its-kind role, you'll set direction, influence engineering culture, and create learnings that may inform both our internal engineering and n8n's product thinking.

Sound like a challenge you're excited to take on?

Apply now, and help us build the future of automation.

n8n is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We can sponsor visas to Germany; for any other country, you need to have existing right to work.

Our company language is English.

You care about diversity and inclusion? We do too! Check out our Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging initiatives at n8n (https://www.notion.so/n8n/Diversity-inclusion-and-belonging-n8n-c1bec2fff536422d868b1a438d990e35).

Location disclaimer: If you see multiple job postings for the same role, it is most likely because we're hiring remotely for this role and posting in different locations to make sure every potential candidate can see the role. Please apply to the location you're the most likely to work from in the future.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation 💸 – We offer fair and attractive pay.

  • Ownership 💪 – Our core value is to “empower others,” and we mean it—you’ll get a slice of n8n with equity.

  • Work/life balance 🏖️ – We work hard but ensure you have time to recharge:

    • Europe: 30 days of vacation, plus public holidays wherever you are.

title: Staff Product Designer
descriptionHtml:
Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About Frontier

Faculty Frontier™ is a decision operating system. It puts AI to work on the decisions that matter most to large organisations, such as where to invest, how to allocate resources, and when to act.

Every enterprise is investing heavily in AI, but few are confident it will improve performance. Too often it goes to what’s easy to automate, disconnected from the decisions that actually move the business.

Frontier works backwards from objectives like revenue, margin and risk to the decisions that drive them, then connects the data, models and agents those decisions need into a world model of the business. Teams simulate and optimise options with ADA, our AI decision agent, and every decision is tracked against its outcome so the system keeps learning. Our ambition is to make business decisions as easy to navigate as getting around a city.

We don’t believe in AI that thinks for people. We believe in AI that helps people think, with humans and agents working together inside a decision system.

Customers start with one high-value decision and prove value in weeks. Over months they connect it into a wider decision network, and over years they build an adaptive enterprise.

Frontier is built by Faculty, an AI company that has delivered more than 400 systems since 2014 and is now part of Accenture.

About Design at Frontier

We’re a small team, growing deliberately - we’d rather have five designers who trust each other than fifteen who don't.

We're tightly integrated with engineering. We prototype in code. We co-own the design system with developers. We're actively exploring what agentic-augmented design work looks like in practice, not in think pieces — and we're honest when we don't have the answer yet.

We’re active in shaping the product culture at Frontier; putting people first, raising the quality bar and ensuring a coherent experience. You’ll be part of shaping that culture.

About the role

You'll be one of the most senior designers on Frontier, shaping a product that's still early enough that the decisions you make will define how it works for years.

Day to day, you'll be designing the surfaces where people and agents collaborate on real clinical decisions — how evidence gets surfaced, how recommendations get explained, how humans push back, how teams learn. This is hard, unsolved design work. The existing patterns for AI interfaces mostly come from consumer chat products; they don't transfer cleanly to environments where the cost of a bad decision is measured in years of research or patient outcomes.

You'll be expected to work end-to-end: from framing the problem with product and engineering, through prototyping in code and design canvases, through shipping. You'll help set the craft bar for the team, mentor the designers around you, and push back when something isn't good enough yet.

What you'll work on

  • Designing the core interaction patterns for how humans and agents collaborate inside a decision loop.

  • Making dense, analytical information legible for expert users who need to trust it, challenge it, and act on it.

  • Shaping the shared design language and system that lets a small team move quickly without the product fragmenting.

  • Partnering with engineering from day one of any problem, not from handoff.

  • Raising the bar for craft — through your own work, through critique, and through the standards you hold the team to.

We think you'll do well here if

  • You've shipped complex software for expert users, in a domain where getting it wrong has real consequences.

  • You design end-to-end and care about the pixels as much as the strategy.

  • You've done serious work on AI or other non-deterministic systems and have opinions about what works and what doesn't.

  • You're comfortable prototyping in code, or motivated to get there.

  • You're direct, kind, and can hold a clear point of view without needing to be the loudest in the room.

  • You want the people who use your product to have better working lives because of it.

You might not enjoy this role if

  • You want to work on a mature product with established patterns. Frontier is early, and the ambiguity is real.

  • You prefer to work handoff-style, away from engineers.

  • You're looking for a role where design sets direction in isolation from product and engineering. We work as one team.

Interview process

  1. Intro call with our talent team (30 min)

  2. Conversation with Duncan, VP of Design (60 min)

  3. Portfolio and case study deep-dive (90 min)

  4. Final conversation with a cross-functional leader (60 min)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

title: Staff Product Engineer - AI Native
descriptionHtml:
Ready to be part of the Legal Tech revolution?

Vision:

As a leading software-as-a-service (SaaS) provider, DiliTrust is a global company dedicated to offering an integrated suite of legal and governance products. Our vision is to digitize legal departments worldwide. With an annual growth rate of over 40% since 2020, our ambition is to become the world's leading Legal Tech company, aiming for a valuation exceeding $1 billion by 2026.

Our Impact:

From generating General Meeting reports to leveraging AI-assisted contract lifecycle management, our teams in our 8 offices across France, the US, Mexico, MEA, Germany, Spain, Italy, and Canada are the driving force behind our global success. We proudly support 2,400 customers in 64 countries, with 80% of our clientele comprising listed companies in major markets such as Europe, North America, and the Middle East.

Our Recognition:

DiliTrust has been at the forefront of Legal Tech innovation, being the first Legal Tech with AI features since 2022. The company is renowned for providing a positive and entrepreneurial work environment. We are honored to have received the "Happy at Work" and "Tech at Work" labels every year since 2019.

The Role:

Lini is DiliTrust's proprietary AI engine, powering Ask Lini, Risk Detector, Document Summarization, Minute Generation, and every AI capability across the suite.

We are building a dedicated squad around it and are looking for a strong Software / Product Engineer, with a focus our platform architecture, to help us bring it to the next level.

As a Software Engineer work at the intersection of AI, product, and engineering. You will contribute to building, improving, and scaling the features that make Lini a reliable and powerful AI layer across the entire DiliTrust suite.

We are looking for an engineer who writes clean, production-ready code and is comfortable taking ownership of features end-to-end, from technical design to deployment. We also care about how you think about AI: whether you bring genuine curiosity to the product, and whether you can translate a model capability into a great user experience.

Missions

  • Write specifications as the durable asset of the project. Executable acceptance criteria, and — crucially — the non-functional requirements that specs almost never carry: data classification, endpoint × role authorization matrix, volumetry assumptions, latency and throughput budgets. These are the requirements whose later correction is superlinear, so they get decided before generation, not after.
  • Freeze the contracts before any fan-out. API schemas, types, module boundaries, invariants. Agents do not negotiate an interface in the hallway: each will make a plausible and incompatible assumption, discovered at integration.
  • Pilot coding agents with a tight brief and a bounded context — narrow tasks, defined input and output artifacts, explicit stop conditions and budgets, full traceability of what produced each change.
  • Keep producer and verifier separate. You do not sign off alone on generation you piloted, and you act as independent verifier on your peers' slices — with an adversarial brief ("find what breaks against this spec"), never "confirm this looks fine".
  • Build the asymmetric gates that make the slice safe at volume — expensive to satisfy, cheap to check: property tests, contract tests, query-count and allocation budgets, execution-plan checks, policy-as-code, backward-compatibility proofs. Written before the implementation exists, so the agent closes the feedback loop itself without consuming human attention.
  • Use code reading as a calibration instrument, not as a gate. Sample deliberately, by risk zone, to measure the real defect rate of the generator-plus-gates pair and to keep the team's mental model of its own system alive.
  • Keep work-in-progress low. Capped PR size, thin vertical slices, trunk-based with very short branches, feature flags over long-lived branches, CI as the agent's first task rather than its last. More features in flight does not mean faster delivery when the bottleneck is verification.
  • Design for blast radius. Reversibility, progressive delivery, structured logs, traces, metrics and instrumentation generated as a matter of course. On many paths, detecting in five minutes beats three days of review that prevents nothing.

Requirements

Being based in France with full working rights. Fluent in French and English.

Experience & Seniority:

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a significant portion spent building and operating B2B SaaS platforms in production
  • Proven ownership of features across their full lifecycle — design, delivery, iteration, maintenance — on long-lived, multi-year products
  • Strong background in complex, scalable web architectures, including real modularity: you have seen where coupling stops parallel work dead

AI-Native Practice:

  • Demonstrated, sustained use of coding agents in production work — not autocomplete, but delegated implementation with review and accountability
  • A concrete, articulated view of where generated code fails: correlated defects rather than idiosyncratic ones, uniform surface quality that destroys the usual "look here" review signals, plausibility with no author to interrogate
  • Comfort being accountable for code you did not author, and the discipline to refuse a change you cannot explain

Verification & Quality:

  • Real fluency in property-based testing, contract testing, and deriving tests from the specification rather than from the code
  • Test-data strategy, including maintaining a volumetrically representative dataset as part of the verification apparatus — not a nice-to-have
  • Instinct for the difference between a rigorous check and a scalable one: does the cost of checking grow with the volume produced?

Security & Performance (non-negotiable on this role):

  • Authorization modelling in multi-tenant systems, and why declarative, centrally enforced authorization beats reviewing each endpoint. Generated code reliably checks who you are and regularly forgets whether you are allowed
  • Awareness of the attack surface specific to an agent-assisted pipeline: prompt injection through ticket descriptions, code comments and dependency READMEs; supply-chain risk on hallucinated package names; least privilege for non-human identities; and the most frequent risk of all — production data or proprietary code leaking into the development loop
  • Performance as a measured number rather than a code-reading opinion: query budgets per HTTP request, N+1, unbounded result sets, missing indexes on new query paths, network calls in loops, execution-plan review. These are invisible at test-data scale and expensive in production

Product & Team Collaboration:

  • Excellent written communication — specification writing is now a core engineering skill on this role, not documentation overhead
  • Extensive experience working directly with product managers, designers and stakeholders in a product-oriented setup
  • Strong sense of ownership and sound judgment on risk: what to build, what not to build, what residual risk is acceptable and why

Education:

  • Master's degree in Engineering or equivalent practical experience in senior SaaS environments

What this role is not

We would rather say it up front:

  • It is not a prompt-engineering role, and it is not an ML/LLM research role.
  • It is not a role where green tests are sufficient evidence. On security and performance, "the spec is met and the tests pass" is not a weak signal — it is a null one.
  • It is not a ticket queue. The profile that shrinks in an AI-native team is the one whose value was implementing assigned tickets between two boundaries.

Our Tech Stack

  • Backend: Node.js / TypeScript
  • Frontend: Vue.js 3
  • Database: PostgreSQL, MariaDB
  • DevOps: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform
  • Cloud: GCP

Engineering apparatus you will use and help build: coding agents orchestrated deterministically in CI, aspect-scoped verification agents (authorization, performance, spec conformance, dependencies), policy-as-code, property-based and contract testing, volumetric test datasets, load and endurance gates on critical paths, feature flags, progressive delivery and end-to-end tracing.

What we offer

  • Join a fast-growing company in a friendly, international environment — engineering primarily in Paris, with further engineering presence in Berlin, Montreal and Wilmington (DE), and offices across France, Italy, Spain, Germany, Canada, the USA, Mexico and Dubai;
  • Our "Remote Policy" guarantees that you can find the right balance between "Onsite" and "Remote";
  • Last but not least, all the day-to-day benefits of the CSE, luncheon vouchers, profit sharing bonuses, etc...

Recruitment process

  • Interview with a TA team member (30/45 mins)
  • Interview with the Engineering Manager (1h)
  • Technical interview (1h30) — two parts: turning an ambiguous requirement into a specification with executable acceptance criteria, then an adversarial review of an agent-generated diff against that specification
  • Interview with the CTO (45 mins)

title: Staff Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Hi 👋 I’m Rich Ashworth, Director of Engineering at hyperexponential.

I lead the Model Authoring value stream that owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models. An actuary might start with an Excel rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved, and is pricing live business. Our job is to turn that into an exceptional user experience and make every step of that credible enough to trust.

I'm hiring a Staff Product Engineer to help set our technical direction and build the next version of our products. It's an individual contributor role, but influence is a huge part of it: the standards the pods work to, the shared enablers underneath the product, and the interfaces where our problems meet other teams'. You’ll be hands-on where the risk is highest.

There's no established playbook for any of this, but there’s an incredible opportunity in front of us. If this sounds like a role that would excite you, I'd love to hear from you.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Model Authoring team

Model Authoring owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models: the model developer experience and our actuarial agent. An actuary might start with an Excel-based rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved and is pricing live business. Our job is to make every step of that credible enough to trust. The team is distributed across our Warsaw and London offices.

As the Staff Product Engineer, you will help set the team's technical direction. This is an individual contributor role, but influence is a large part of it: you'll help define the standards the team works to, raise the technical bar across pods, and own the interfaces where our problems meet those of teams elsewhere in Technology. You'll be expected to move fast and start shaping technical conversations early. We work in an AI-native way, and you'll help define and evolve what that means here.

What you'll be doing

  • Establish a set of engineering standards across the Model Authoring pods. The standards are documented and actively referenced in code review, with new pod work conforming by default.

  • Set and own the technical direction for the team's shared enablers, including how we represent and persist models, the model registry, secure context access, and shared agentic infrastructure.

  • Establish the technical interfaces between Model Authoring and other parts of the business. Dependencies with other teams are agreed, documented, and progressing without needing to be brokered by someone else.

  • Work hands-on on the hardest problems in the stream. This is not an advisory role: we would expect you in the code where the risk is highest.

  • Help define how we work in an AI-native way. Which parts of model development and of our own engineering we hand to agents, what stays human, and what evidence we need before trusting either.

  • Visibly lift the engineers around you. You're sought out for design input across pods, and there's at least one engineer whose growth is clearly attributable to your support.

What you'll need to have done

  • Worked in an AI-native environment, and genuinely want to keep doing so. You've used AI or agentic tools in your own engineering workflow, introduced or experimented with them, and have a real view on what's worked and what hasn't.

  • Been product-focused rather than purely technical. You understand who your users are, where their pain points are, and how your technical decisions connect to commercial outcomes.

  • Set technical direction while navigating genuine ambiguity. A proven track record of owning architecture in a domain with no established playbook, and making clear calls on imperfect information rather than deferring them.

  • Owned a significant technical challenge or service end to end, with the depth to walk through it in detail - the trade-offs, the contracts, the things you'd do differently.

  • Influenced across teams. You can hold a position under challenge, genuinely listen to pushback, and persuade others - not just present your own view and hope it lands.

  • Worked effectively across distributed teams - this role spans our Warsaw and London offices, so you'll need to be comfortable building relationships and influence across both.

You're unlikely to thrive here if

  • You'd rather focus purely on the technical problem than get close to users, customer pain points, and the commercial implications of what you build.

  • You're not comfortable setting technical direction in ambiguity, or you'd rather wait for an established playbook than make a call on imperfect information.

  • You're not excited about helping define what the future of software engineering looks like and are prepared to embrace tooling and new ways of working to support this.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

  1. Initial call with our Talent team

  2. Hiring Manager Interview

  3. Skills Assessment & follow-up interview

  4. Values Interview

  5. Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

title: Staff Product Manager, AI Agents & Assistant
descriptionHtml:
About Dashlane

Dashlane’s mission is to deliver the credential security every business and employee needs to thrive. Millions of consumers, and over 25,000 brands worldwide, such as Michelin, Air France, and Forrester, trust Dashlane for industry-leading innovations, patented zero-knowledge security, and an unmatched user experience. Founded in Paris, Dashlane has since established offices in New York and Lisbon, and has grown to more than 300 Dashlaners globally.

We're looking for people who actively use AI tools to drive efficiency, creativity, and impact in their work. At Dashlane, we drive innovation and value learning, strive for excellence in everything we do, and thrive as one team. Learn more about life at Dashlane, including how we work, how we hire, and the benefits of being a Dashlaner.

About the role

As our Staff Product Manager for Agentic Capabilities, you will own the vision, strategy and roadmap for how Dashlane becomes an interface for AI agents and assistants for consumers and businesses. Success means people hand real, valuable tasks to agents through Dashlane and keep doing it, and companies trust it enough to let their teams do the same.

You will own the product alongside senior engineers as a Staff-level individual contributor in a 0-to-1 role where standards are still unsettled. We are looking for strong familiarity with the modern AI landscape, including LLMs, assistants and agentic workflows, and sound judgment about what agents can and cannot be trusted with.

At Dashlane, we embrace a hybrid culture that combines the best of both worlds: the creativity and energy of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Our model is designed to strengthen team connections while supporting individual productivity and work-life balance. To maximize collaboration, we come together in the office on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays, while Wednesdays and Fridays offer more flexibility for focused work.

Key Responsibilities

  • Set the direction. Form and defend a point of view on how agents and assistants should act with what Dashlane protects, for consumers and businesses, and turn it into a strategy, positioning, and multi-year plan that leadership will back.

  • Read the market and judge readiness. Keep a living view of how agent makers, assistants, browsers, identity vendors and password managers are moving. Assess how ready emerging pieces such as passkeys for agents and agent sign-in standards are, and set the triggers for acting on each.

  • Own the evidence. Run discovery on the jobs people hand to agents at home and at work. Establish who hands over real tasks and what holds them back, so your bets follow demand, not hype.

  • Connect consumer and business. Treat both as a connected problem. Turn what we learn from individuals handing tasks to agents into the visibility and controls that IT and Security teams need to govern agent access at work. Flag when a decision for one audience affects the other.

  • Own the trust commitment. Define what Dashlane promises about what an agent or model can see and do, and hold every product decision and release to that promise. Turn what agents can and cannot be trusted with into a set of durable product primitives, such as limits, approvals, records and revocation, that stay valid as agents change.

  • Shape our place in the ecosystem. Decide which agent makers and platforms we invest in and on what terms. Build the relationships and technical case that make Dashlane an easy yes for them, and for the services agents log in to. Lead Dashlane’s input to the standards that govern how agents sign in and act on someone’s behalf, so our positions reflect real customer needs and our product direction.

  • Own the numbers. Set baselines and targets for adoption, repeat use and trust, including time to a first approved agent login, how long people take to decide on an agent’s request, and how often failures are recovered without the person starting over. Be accountable for them to leadership.

  • Align the organization. Bring Design, Engineering, Security, Legal, Sales & Marketing towards one plan, establish the operating rhythm and decision framework for the team, and settle ownership where it is unclear.

In your first year:

  • By 90 days, the team's early engineering work has become a shared view of the problem, a trust model that Security and Architecture back, and proposed targets for what "working" means. You have shared a point of view on the category with Dashlane leadership.

  • By 6 months, real people are experiencing agentic value through Dashlane, engagement is recurring, and you know who gets the most value first.

  • By 12 months, people keep using it and it shows in who chooses and stays on our plans. A version for companies has a clear first slice, and you have a view on where to go next. You have a vision and roadmap for agents and assistants across B2B and B2C that leadership has backed.

Requirements

  • 8+ years in product management, including ownership of an authentication, security, identity or permissions-heavy product, and at least one product you took from zero to market with measurable success (adoption, revenue or retention) in a market that was still emerging.

  • Enough technical fluency (OAuth, passkeys, sessions, browser extensions) to follow a token-flow discussion with engineers and ask where it breaks. You don't need to write code but you must be comfortable with speaking the language of engineering.

  • Strong familiarity with the modern AI landscape, including LLMs, assistants and agentic workflows. The ability to reason about what AI can and cannot do through a product and customer lens, with working knowledge of how agents operate: tool use and standard tool interfaces, browser-driving agents, how context is kept or lost, and where they can be tricked.

  • A track record of reading a fast-moving market and turning its signals into a strategy that leadership acted on.

  • Experience running 0-to-1 discovery with small samples and incomplete information, defining success as customer outcomes rather than shipped features.

  • AI-native ways of working: you build working prototypes with AI, run discovery synthesis through it, chain agents into your own workflow, and can show concretely how it has changed how you “do product”.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English: crisp problem statements, clear 1-pagers, compelling roadmap rationale, and external narratives that shape how a category is understood.

We're Also Looking For

  • Systems thinking and platform experience. You think in systems and have shipped a platform, API, integration product or partner ecosystem that other software relies on, with outcomes you can describe: the baseline, what changed, what you cut.

  • Consumer and business experience. Experience with products that serve both individuals and businesses, and the instinct to flag early how a decision in one ripples into the other.

  • Comfort with ambiguity. You will join a team whose engineers have already started scouting ahead, and you favor action over perfection, deciding with incomplete information.

  • A collaborative spirit and low ego. As comfortable deferring to others' expertise as you are asserting your own point of view.

  • Intellectual honesty. You share results transparently, learn openly from failures, and write down the evidence that would make you move earlier, later or not at all.

  • Security standard for AI. You have a threat-model instinct (prompt injection, phishing, malicious extensions, what a compromised agent could still do) and hold AI to the same standard as security: human accountability at every consequential decision, and evaluation before anything ships.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging at Dashlane:

As a truly international company—founded in France and distributed across France, US and Portugal—Dashlane thrives off diverse perspectives. We value all aspects of diversity: gender identity, sexual orientation, ability, ethnic origin, social background, age, lifestyle, and more. We are committed to hiring a diverse community and fostering a culture where everyone is heard and belongs. See more about this here. 

Your interview experience: 

To know what to expect once you’ve sent your application, read about how we interview and hire at Dashlane. Feel free to browse our blog to find more information about our product and how we work.

title: Staff Safety & Robotics Software Engineer (w/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Deine Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst und implementierst sicherheitskritische Lösungen für autonome Gabelstapler, die in Logistik- und Produktionsumgebungen eingesetzt werden
  • Du überführst Sicherheitskonzepte und Systemanforderungen in robuste Softwarearchitekturen, Safety-PLC-Lösungen und industrielle Steuerungssysteme
  • Du konzipierst, entwickelst und wartest Softwarekomponenten für Robotersteuerung, Bewegungsregelung und autonome Fahrfunktionen
  • Du definierst und führst Verifikations- und Validierungsaktivitäten durch, einschließlich Integrations-, Fault-Injection- und Systemtests
  • Du arbeitest eng mit Functional-Safety-Experten, Systemarchitekten und Softwareentwicklern zusammen, um den sicheren und zuverlässigen Betrieb unserer Systeme sicherzustellen
  • Du agierst als Fachexperte für sicherheitskritische Software- und PLC-Entwicklung, unterstützt Kolleg:innen und förderst Engineering Best Practices im Unternehmen

Dein Profil

  • Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Elektrotechnik, Mechatronik, Informatik, Robotik, Software Engineering oder eines vergleichbaren Fachgebiets
  • Du bringst mindestens 6 Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Entwicklung sicherheitskritischer Software, industrieller Automatisierungssysteme, Robotikanwendungen oder Safety-PLC-Lösungen mit
  • Du verfügst über fundierte Erfahrung mit industriellen Sicherheitssteuerungen oder Safety PLCs; Kenntnisse in Siemens S7 und TIA Portal oder SICK Flexi Soft/Flexi Net sind von großem Vorteil
  • Du hast nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Implementierung und Validierung von Sicherheitsfunktionen gemäß Normen wie ISO 13849, IEC 61508 oder IEC 62061
  • Du besitzt ein gutes Verständnis von Sicherheitskonzepten, Sicherheitsarchitekturen und anforderungsgetriebener Entwicklung
  • Du bist mit Verifikation, Validierung, Anforderungsnachverfolgbarkeit und V-Modell-basierten Entwicklungsprozessen vertraut
  • Du hast Erfahrung in der Integration von Sensoren, Aktoren, industriellen Kommunikationssystemen und Feldbussen, idealerweise CANopen
  • Idealerweise bringst Du Kenntnisse in einem oder mehreren der folgenden Bereiche mit: SICK-Sicherheitslaserscanner, ROS-basierte Robotersysteme, C++- oder Python-Entwicklung, ros_control/ros2_control, Docker oder Motion-Control-Frameworks
  • Du legst Wert auf eine klare technische Dokumentation und den professionellen Umgang mit Versionsverwaltungssystemen
  • Du verfügst über sehr gute Englischkenntnisse und gute Deutschkenntnisse (mindestens B1)
  • Du arbeitest überwiegend vor Ort und wohnst idealerweise im Raum München oder bist bereit, regelmäßig vor Ort zu arbeiten.

Was wir bieten

  • Spitzentechnologie: Als Pioniere der Robotik sind wir in der Lage, ohne Schienen und Leitlinien zu navigieren und zu manipulieren, und bieten Lösungen für Prozesse, die noch nie jemand zuvor automatisieren konnte!
  • Team: Wir sind ein internationales Team mit mehr als 25 Nationalitäten. Du wirst in einem Team mit sehr smarten, bescheidenen, kooperativen und fleißigen Menschen arbeiten.
  • Kultur: Sei einfach Du selbst! Werde Teil eines dynamischen, innovativenund vielfältigen Teams, das Zusammenarbeit über Hierarchie stellt. Um innovativ zu sein, muss man ab und zu scheitern – wir lernen und verbessern uns ständig.
  • Vollverpflegung: Du hast keine Lust, darüber nachzudenken, was du morgen zu Mittag essen willst, geschweige denn, es vorzubereiten? Zum Glück verwöhnt uns unser französischer Koch jeden Tag mit einem frisch gekochten kostenlosen Mittagessen! Und als Sahnehäubchen gibt es einen gefüllten Kühlschrank mit Getränken, frischem Obst und natürlich Kaffee!
  • Flexibilität: Flexibilität wird bei uns großgeschrieben. Unser hybrides Arbeitsmodell für Positionen, bei denen Anwesenheit verzichtbar ist, trägt zu einer gesunden Work-Life-Balance bei.
  • Benefits: Wir bieten attraktive Urlaubs‑, Wellpass‑, Gesundheits- und Vergütungsleistungen. Erfahre hier mehr über unsere aktuellen Benefits.

Du erfüllst nicht alle Anforderungen zu 100 %? Kein Problem. Wir wissen, dass die besten Talente nicht immer jeden Punkt einer Stellenanzeige mitbringen. Wenn Du Dich für Robotik begeisterst und die Zukunft der Automatisierung mitgestalten möchtest, freuen wir uns auf Deine Bewerbung. Vielleicht ist genau diese Position der richtige nächste Schritt für Dich oder eine andere spannende Gelegenheit bei Jungheinrich Robotics.

Für uns bei Jungheinrich Robotics ist die Förderung der Inklusion sehr wichtig. Wir sind daher bestrebt, ein inklusives Umfeld für alle Kandidaten zu schaffen und bieten allen qualifizierten Bewerbern unabhängig von Geschlecht, ethnischer Zugehörigkeit, Alter, nationaler Herkunft, sexueller Orientierung, Kultur oder Bildung gleiche Chancen. Wenn Du gewisse Anpassungen benötigst, um den Rekruitingprozess für Dich zugänglich zu machen, werden wir unser Bestes tun, um Dir entgegenzukommen. Sprich uns gerne darauf an!

Présentation générale

Gemmyo est une Maison de joaillerie indépendante qui développe une nouvelle vision du luxe, ancrée dans son époque.

Les créations sont conçues et fabriquées en France à la commande et proposées dans une vaste sélection de pierres et de métaux précieux. La marque se distingue par une expérience client personnalisée, un modèle largement digital, une distribution 100% intégrée, et des prix toujours respectueux.

Plus de la moitié des ventes sont réalisées sur le site internet Gemmyo et le reste à travers les 9 boutiques de la marque, situées à Paris (2 boutiques), Lyon, Aix-en-Provence, Bordeaux, Toulouse, Genève, Bruxelles et Tokyo. La Maison est également présente via une Résidence (boutique éphémère) à Zurich depuis juillet 2024.

La Maison d’une centaine de collaborateurs est aujourd’hui référente pour une clientèle francophone exigeante.

Entreprise autofinancée et rentable, Gemmyo souhaite accélérer son développement à l’international.   • Vous aimez prendre des initiatives

  • Vous êtes organisé.e et rigoureux.se

  • Vous aimez la gestion, la coordination et le suivi de projet

  • Vous aimez faire preuve d’imagination et faire face aux imprévus

  • Vous êtes d’un naturel curieux.se et aimez découvrir de nouvelles personnalités publiques

  • Vous parlez et écrivez anglais

  • Présence à Paris nécessaire pour un travail sur place avec les autres équipes Gemmyo.

Avantages

  • Opportunité unique de se plonger au cœur d’une entreprise en fort développement, qui insuffle une bouffée d’air frais dans un secteur souvent enfoncé dans ses certitudes.

Vous contribuerez directement au rayonnement de la marque à travers des événements d’envergure, des collaborations inspirantes et des rencontres avec des personnalités du monde du luxe

  • Environnement de travail dynamique, bienveillant, avec un engagement fort sur le management.

descriptionHtml:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacuna l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École.

Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques.

Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret.

Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité.

Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins.

L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité.

🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’industrie du futur.

Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ?

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

La production de béton est responsable d'environ 8 % des émissions mondiales de CO2. Ces émissions sont principalement liées à la combustion et à la décarbonatation du calcaire nécessaire à la production du ciment Portland conventionnel.

Les liants à base de magnésie (MgO) sont étudiés comme alternatives potentielles aux ciments conventionnels, avec une empreinte carbone réduite. Le magnésium nécessaire à leur production pourrait être extrait de roches non carbonatées ou de saumures riches en magnésium. Ces ressources constituent des sources alternatives de matières premières et pourraient permettre d'éviter les émissions de CO2 liées à la décarbonatation du calcaire.

Cependant, ces liants alternatifs sont encore en cours de développement et leurs mécanismes d'hydratation, leur composition et leurs propriétés mécaniques doivent être mieux compris. En particulier, la nature et la réactivité de la source de magnésium, ainsi que les conditions de formulation et de préparation, peuvent influencer la microstructure et les performances mécaniques du matériau obtenu.

L'objectif de ce stage est d'étudier différentes sources de magnésium et d'évaluer leur potentiel pour le développement de liants de type MgO-SiO2 présentant de bonnes propriétés mécaniques et un impact environnemental réduit.

Plusieurs formulations de liants seront préparées et étudiées en faisant varier la source de magnésium et différents paramètres de formulation. Les matériaux obtenus seront caractérisés à l'aide de techniques complémentaires afin d'évaluer leur composition chimique, les phases formées lors de l'hydratation, leur microstructure, leur porosité et leurs propriétés mécaniques. Les principales étapes du stage seront les suivantes :

· Étude bibliographique : synthèse des connaissances sur les liants magnésiens, leurs mécanismes d'hydratation et leurs applications potentielles.

· Caractérisation des matières premières : étude de la composition chimique et minéralogique, de la distribution granulométrique (PSD) et de la réactivité des matières premières sélectionnées.

· Formulation et préparation des liants : élaboration de pâtes de ciment de type MgO-SiO2 en utilisant différentes sources de magnésium et différents paramètres de préparation.

· Caractérisation des matériaux : analyse des pâtes hydratées par diffraction des rayons X (DRX), analyse thermogravimétrique (ATG), microscopie électronique à balayage couplée à la spectroscopie à dispersion d'énergie (MEB/EDS), mesure de la porosité accessible à l'eau et essais mécaniques.

Analyse des résultats : comparaison des différentes formulations afin d'identifier les principaux paramètres influençant leur microstructure et leurs propriétés mécaniques.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Étudiant(e) en Master 2 ou en dernière année d'école d'ingénieurs, spécialisé(e) en génie civil, science des matériaux ou domaine connexe.

🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ?

Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde.

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est l’opportunité de trouver :

· Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un réseau international solide (T.I.M.E., EULIST) et des campus à taille humaine avec un environnement urbain

· Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an

Construisons un avenir plus durable, à travers la science, l’ingénierie, et des projets qui font sens.

Contexte
Notre portail développeur tourne sous Backstage, et la conformité de nos composants y est aujourd'hui contrôlée par un plugin communautaire. Celui-ci est monolithique et limité à ce que Backstage connaît, c'est-à-dire les composants déclarés dans son catalogue. Tout le reste du SI — code source hors catalogue, ressources cloud, métriques — n'est contrôlé automatiquement par personne. title: Stage M2 : Recherche en optique non linéaire appliquée à la caractérisation de dispositifs électroniques neuromorphiques - 6 mois
descriptionHtml:
Mines Saint-Etienne est une Ecole de l’Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT), 1er groupe public d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management en France. L’IMT est un EPSCP (grand établissement) sous la tutelle du Ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique.

L’École Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Saint-Étienne (Mines Saint-Etienne) est chargée de missions de formation, de recherche et d’innovation, de transfert vers l’industrie et de culture scientifique, technique et industrielle.

Mines Saint-Etienne représente: 2 400 élèves-ingénieurs et chercheurs en formation, 480 personnels (150 Chercheurs et Enseignants-chercheurs), un budget consolidé de 46 M€, 3 campus dédiés à l’industrie à Saint-Etienne et Lyon (région AURA), à la microélectronique et aux objets connectés à Gardanne (Métropole Aix-Marseille Provence, région SUD) et à l’ingénierie pour la santé à Saint-Etienne ; 6 unités de recherche ; 5 centres de formation et de recherche ; un centre de culture scientifique technique et industrielle leader en France « La Rotonde » (> 50 000 visiteurs / an).

Contexte scientifique et objectifs du stage :

Des dispositifs d’électronique organique ultra-flexibles, conformables et implantables incorporant une intelligence artificielle promettent de révolutionner la surveillance et le traitement en temps réel de maladies chroniques [1]. De tels systèmes pourraient être basés sur des transistors organiques électrochimiques (OECTs), exploitant des conducteurs polymères mixtes ion-électron (PMIECs) comme couches actives. En effet, les PMIECs sont apparus comme une excellente plateforme matérielle pour interfacer la biologie avec l’électronique conventionnelle ; identifié comme le domaine de la « bioélectronique organique ou plastique ». L’OECT est considéré comme l’éléments clé pour réaliser une telle interface [2]. Son efficacité est évaluée suivant des figures de mérite (FoMs) telles que i) la transconductance (gm), et/ou ii) les temps de commutation (ionique vs. électronique) dans le dispositif. Au-delà des applications de transduction, à court terme, l’OECT est aussi intéressant pour créer des applications émergentes en matière de circuits neuromorphiques bioélectroniques [3].

La réalisation de tels circuits est freinée par un manque de compréhension et d’optimisation des processus de conduction mixte dans ces matériaux polymériques ; notamment une asymétrie des temps de commutation des transistors lors des séquences de dopage (i.e « ON ») vs dédopage (i.e « OFF ») dans le canal de l’OECT. Des outils de caractérisation in-situ & operando permettant de quantifier et cartographier les paramètres de transduction électronique et électrochimique dans le canal de l’OECT se révèlent être indispensables pour comprendre les limitations actuelles en performances des PMIECs et/ou pour construire des PMIECs optimums dans de tels circuits neuromorphiques.

Dans ce contexte scientifique, le.la stagiaire développera une nouvelle mesure de spectroscopie et instrumentation d’optique non linéaire, appelée microscopie par génération de second harmonique résolue en temps, afin d’enregistrer le mouvement spatio-temporel des espèces chargées, ion et électrons (ou trous), et ainsi donc cartographier les mobilités électroniques in-situ & operando le canal de l’OECT.

La.le stagiaire fabriquera ces dispositifs OECTs en salle blanche de microélectronique, et bénéficiera d’un accompagnement technique pour leur réalisation. Il.elle enregistrera et analysera les FoMs clés grâce à l'expérimentation d’optique non linéaire développée et aux caractérisations électriques et électrochimiques afin d’établir, de manière plus globale, des règles d’ingénierie dans ces PMIECs qui serviront de socle de connaissances incontournables à l’avenir, pour mettre en œuvre et appliquer des circuits neuromorphiques à base d'OECTs, comme première brique d’une intelligence artificielle d’électronique organique.

Pour aller plus loin :

[1] https://iconic.mines-stetienne.fr/

[2] https://doi.org/10.1038/ s43586-021-00065-8

[3] https://www.nature.com/articles/s41578-023-00622-5

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

La candidate ou le candidat devra être en cours de formation et d’apprentissage d’un diplôme de Master 2 ou de 3ème année de diplôme d’ingénieurs en Techniques Optiques et Instrumentations. La candidate ou le candidat devra disposer d’une culture solide en Physique/ Science des Matériaux/ (Opto)Électronique par sa formation initiale et/ou son expérience professionnelle.

Ce sujet de stage M2 Recherche a vocation d’être poursuivi en cycle de doctorat. Seul.e un.e étudiant.e intéressé.e pour continuer en doctorat sera donc retenu.e pour ce stage.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Les principaux critères d’évaluation du candidat seront les suivants (liste non exhaustive) :

  • Maitrise technique et scientifique en Optique. Des expériences lors de précédents stages en optique non linéaire et/ou microscopie, analyse d’images par caméra scientifique sera considéré comme avantageuses,

  • Maitrise d’instrumentation électronique (caméra sCMOS, oscilloscope, générateur de signaux et à délai, SMU,…) et d’analyse d’images sous ordinateur (Python, …),

  • Aptitudes pour le travail interdisciplinaire et les collaborations pluridisciplinaires.

  • Autonomie, initiative,

  • Intérêt pour le travail en équipe et capacité à construire un projet de recherche dans ce contexte,

title: Stage Sales Backoffice
descriptionHtml:
Op zoek naar een stage waar je écht meedraait in een team en veel leert over hoe een snelgroeiende organisatie werkt? Dan hebben wij een mooie plek voor je. My Jewellery zoekt een enthousiaste en proactieve stagiair(e) die ons sales team komt versterken van februari 2027 t/m juli 2027.

Tijdens deze stage werk je mee op onze sales backoffice en krijg je een goed beeld van hoe het er achter de schermen aan toegaat bij een snelgroeiend fashion brand.

Je bent binnen de backoffice echt een spin in het web: je hebt contact met verschillende afdelingen zoals sales, logistiek, finance en klantenservice. Hierdoor leer je hoe alles binnen een organisatie met elkaar samenhangt en krijg je een brede kijk op het commerciële proces. Daarnaast krijg je de mogelijkheid om tijdens je stage 1 à 2 dagen mee te kijken op andere afdelingen.

Wat je gaat doen

  • Je ondersteunt de backoffice van de salesafdeling;

  • Je houdt je bezig met het invoeren van orders;

  • Je helpt mee met het coördineren van de samples;

  • Je denkt mee over hoe processen binnen de afdeling slimmer of beter kunnen;

  • Je bent proactief en ondersteunt het team op verschillende vlakken waar nodig.


  • Je studeert in de richting van fashion, commercie of sales;

  • Je bent van februari 2027 t/m juli 2027 beschikbaar;

  • Je bent beschikbaar voor 32 tot 38 uur per week;

  • Jij bent proactief en bent iemand die zelf actie onderneemt;

  • Een creatieve geest en oog voor detail zijn belangrijk.

Over ons

Vandaag de dag is My Jewellery met een ambitieus, toegewijd en gedreven team een van de snelst groeiende e-commerce bedrijven van Nederland. Elke dag werken wij met meer dan 1000 medewerkers om een merk te creëren dat het beste van ons allemaal vertegenwoordigt. Bij My Jewellery draait het om jou. Zolang jij groeit, groeien wij met jou mee, want wij geloven namelijk dat iedereen een bijzonder talent heeft en proberen de plek te zijn waar je dit zo optimaal mogelijk kunt ontplooien.

We zijn van origine een Brabants bedrijf en dat merk je aan de gemoedelijke en betrokken sfeer onder collega’s. Je kan helemaal jezelf zijn en de focus ligt op: blijven leren en ontwikkelen. Je krijgt het volledige vertrouwen om projecten op te pakken, ook als dat nieuw voor je is. Wij zijn een platte organisatie, gemakkelijk in de omgang en waar iedereen helemaal zichzelf kan zijn.

Met oog voor elkaar, onze klanten, leveranciers en omgeving, blijven wij stappen zetten naar verdere groei in binnen- en buitenland. Let’s grow together!

title: Strategy & Operations Lead
descriptionHtml:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

You will work closely with core teams on the highest impact initiatives across engineering, product, hiring, operations, and business development. As the company grows, you'll help solve new challenges, build new capabilities, and drive execution wherever it matters most.

We're looking for people who learn quickly, think deeply, and enjoy solving difficult problems in a fast-moving environment.

What You'll Own

  • Drive high-priority initiatives across the business.

  • Work with leadership to solve business and product challenges.

  • Build new teams, processes, and capabilities as the company grows.

  • Lead cross-functional projects from planning through execution.

  • Research new markets, products, and business opportunities.

  • Improve how we operate by identifying problems and implementing practical solutions.

  • Take ownership of projects and deliver meaningful business outcomes.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong problem-solving skills and business judgment.

  • Ability to learn quickly and adapt to new challenges.

  • Comfortable working across different business functions.

  • Strong ownership and execution skills.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

  • Able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment.

  • Curious, resourceful, and driven to build.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only want to attend meetings.

  • Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

  • Those who need fixed scope and slow timelines.

  • People who avoid messy cross-functional problems.

  • People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions


Location

  • This role is based in the United Kingdom. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our United Kingdom office at least 3 days per week.


Language

  • English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.


Interview Process:

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process.

Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Systems Simulation & Performance Modelling - Member of Technical Staff
descriptionHtml:
About Us

We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.

Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.

The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.

Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.

Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.

In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.

We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

Callosum believes that scaling heterogeneous AI infrastructure requires understanding how emerging hardware will behave as part of larger computational systems. Performance characteristics measured on individual accelerators rarely translate directly to distributed deployments, where networking, memory, and execution strategies introduce new constraints. We are developing simulation infrastructure that allows us to explore these interactions and evaluate future systems before they exist.

This role advances the simulation and performance modelling tools that inform Callosum's hardware and infrastructure decisions. You will extend models that project device-level performance to rack-scale systems, explore alternative hardware configurations and execution strategies, and provide experimental environments for automated optimisation. The work also encompasses profiling, workload tracing, and performance instrumentation, connecting measurements from real systems to accurate and useful models of those we want to build.

What You'll Build

  • Extend our simulators to predict heterogeneous compute performance from individual accelerators to multi-rack deployments.

  • Model networking, memory, and execution behaviour to evaluate alternative system architectures and configurations.

  • Develop profiling, tracing, and workload capture tools that inform and validate simulation models.

  • Extend simulation environments for rapid experimentation and automated optimisation of systems and algorithms.

  • Characterise emerging accelerator architectures and translate hardware measurements into predictive models of system-level performance.

What Sets You Apart

  • Strong experience in systems simulation, performance modelling, or performance-critical systems software.

  • Deep understanding of computer architecture, distributed systems, or high-performance computing.

  • Familiarity with profiling, tracing, instrumentation, and methods for characterising computational workloads.

  • Strong systems programming experience, ideally including C++ or Rust.

  • Ability to reason about modelling accuracy, abstraction, and trade-offs between simulation fidelity and computational cost.

What We Offer

  • Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience

  • Equity & Ownership

  • Private healthcare

  • We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

  • We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us

We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome, and believe in equal opportunities for all.
